statement: Critical and near-critical XY scaling and BKT universality. For the square-lattice nearest-neighbor cosine XY model, proves critical axis correlations $`C_{\beta_c}(r)\sim Ar^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}`$ and the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity $`\sqrt{\beta_c-\beta}\log\xi(\beta)\to B`$, with $`A,B\gt 0`$ after the free-box thermodynamic limit. For finite square-symmetric interactions containing nearest neighbors, discrete Gaussian heights converge to Gaussian fields throughout the rough phase, including its threshold, along geometric torus sizes. Critical center-magnetization and spin-field conclusions retain their stated height, renormalization, and field-input assumptions.
